title: Agent Sandboxing & Capability Isolation
summary: Constrain agent-executed code and tools through independent process, filesystem, network, credential, and resource boundaries.
overview: Sandboxing limits what an untrusted or compromised execution can affect. For agents, the risk includes generated code, third-party tools, retrieved instructions, and ordinary mistakes. Capability isolation grants only the particular files, endpoints, operations, and resources required for the current task.

A prompt telling the model to behave safely is not an isolation boundary. Enforcement belongs below the model in operating-system controls, container or virtual-machine boundaries, network policy, scoped service adapters, and credential brokers. The appropriate isolation strength depends on the trust level and the consequences of a boundary escape.

production.poc: A proof of concept may run generated analysis in a disposable environment using synthetic files and no ambient production credentials.
production.production: Production requires explicit mounts, outbound network policy, nonprivileged execution, resource limits, ephemeral credentials, and validated artifact export paths.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds workload classes with different isolation strength, tenant placement policy, sandbox lifecycle controls, patching, escape testing, and capacity accounting.

components.name: Task capability manifest
components.role: Declares permitted inputs, outputs, endpoints, operations, and resource budgets for one execution.

components.name: Sandbox launcher
components.role: Creates an isolated process environment with constrained privileges and a disposable filesystem.

components.name: Credential broker
components.role: Issues short-lived operation-scoped credentials without exposing broad secrets to generated code.

components.name: Network and tool gateway
components.role: Enforces approved destinations, methods, resource scope, and request limits.

components.name: Artifact verifier
components.role: Inspects outputs before copying accepted artifacts into trusted storage or presenting them to users.

flow.title: Classify execution
flow.description: Determine whether the task runs trusted adapters, generated code, or third-party binaries and choose a suitable isolation boundary.

flow.title: Compile capabilities
flow.description: Translate authorized intent into concrete mounts, endpoints, operations, and limits; deny unspecified access by default.

flow.title: Launch clean environment
flow.description: Create a fresh sandbox without host secrets, privileged sockets, or inherited writable project directories unless explicitly required.

flow.title: Execute bounded work
flow.description: Run the task with CPU, memory, time, process, and network limits enforced outside model control.

flow.title: Validate exported artifacts
flow.description: Check paths, file types, size, and expected content before promoting outputs into the trusted workspace.

flow.title: Destroy and account
flow.description: Revoke credentials, terminate descendants, remove temporary state, and record resource usage and policy violations.

useCase.title: Client spreadsheet analysis workspace
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A delivery team asks an agent to run generated data-cleaning code on client-provided spreadsheets.
useCase.problem: The code may read unintended host files or transmit client data if it inherits broad filesystem and network access.
useCase.requirement: Permit analysis of approved inputs and export of reviewed results while isolating client data and execution resources.
useCase.architecture: Each job receives read-only input mounts, a private scratch directory, no default network access, and a controlled artifact export service.
useCase.failure: A script tries to access a host credential path; filesystem isolation denies it and the job returns an explicit blocked-access result.
useCase.impact: Measure completed authorized analyses, blocked boundary violations, cleanup success, resource consumption, and artifact validation failures without claiming isolation is infallible.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reduces the reachable host and cross-tenant surface.
tradeoffs.cost: Adds startup latency, operational overhead, and possibly lower utilization.
Tasks needing external data require explicit approved adapters.
Repeated setup can increase latency and package-cache complexity.

failures.scenario: A writable host socket is accidentally mounted.
failures.detection: Launch-policy validation identifies a privileged socket or forbidden mount.
failures.recovery: Reject the sandbox specification and correct the launcher policy before execution.

failures.scenario: A job spawns processes that survive its parent.
failures.detection: Lifecycle accounting detects descendants or resource usage after job completion.
failures.recovery: Terminate the entire workload boundary and verify credential revocation and storage cleanup.

mistakes.mistake: Treating an ordinary container as sufficient for every hostile workload.
mistakes.fix: Choose isolation based on threat model and verify host, kernel, and runtime exposure.

mistakes.mistake: Giving generated code a general cloud credential.
mistakes.fix: Use a broker or adapter that enforces narrow operations and short lifetimes.

mistakes.mistake: Copying every output file back automatically.
mistakes.fix: Validate paths, sizes, types, and content at a separate export boundary.

whenToUse: Agents execute generated code or process untrusted files with complex parsers.
Multiple users or tenants share compute and storage infrastructure.
A workflow needs a concrete enforceable limit on tools, network, and resource use.
whenNotToUse: The task is a pure model response with no execution or external capabilities to constrain.
Required host privileges would nullify the intended isolation boundary.
Safety-critical control requires a separately engineered real-time execution environment.
checklist: Document the threat model and selected process or virtual-machine boundary.
Deny inherited secrets, privileged sockets, and unintended host mounts.
Limit outbound destinations and service operations independently of prompts.
Enforce CPU, memory, process, storage, and elapsed-time budgets.
Use short-lived scoped credentials and test revocation after completion.
Validate artifacts before exporting them to trusted storage.
Test descendant cleanup, cross-tenant access, and sandbox policy bypass attempts.
